WHAT THE TABLE IS: the five items INTRU_1..INTRU_5 are the five LEARNING TRIALS of the Rey Auditory Verbal Learning Test, and resp (0-4) is the COUNT of intrusion errors -- words the participant recalled that were not on the 15-word list -- made on that trial. Confirmed against data/mancone_2024_ravlt.py, which melts the columns INTRU_1..INTRU_5 of the deposit .sav BY NAME (so the IRW code IS the source column name; no positional step, Step 3b clean). WHY NOTHING IS SHIPPABLE, field by field: (a) item_text -- an item here is a trial, not a question; the stimulus is the SAME 15 spoken words at every trial, so there is no per-item wording to transcribe, and nothing IRW could write there would be text a participant read; (b) option_text -- resp is a raw error count on an unlabelled 0-4 range, and padding it with its own number is barred; (c) instructions -- the paper never reproduces the examiner's script, only a third-person procedure description ('In the first task the examiner reads the words and asks the subject to repeat them. After the first task, the words are read another four times...'), which is the authors' prose about the test, not the literal instructions given to the participant, and the administration was Italian (Rey, 1958; Carlesimo et al., 1996) while that prose is English. SOURCES CHECKED AND EXHAUSTED: the PeerJ article text (CC BY 4.0, 10.7717/peerj.18195, cached paper.xml/paper.txt) contains no item list, no word list and no instructions; the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles zip for PMC11470773 holds exactly ten figure images plus one file, peerj-12-18195-s001.sav ('Supplemental Information 1 Raw data' is the article's only supplement); that .sav's variable labels are bare column names ('INTRU_1' -> 'INTRU_1', checked with pyreadstat over all 21 columns) and its value labels cover only gender/group/gaming_prevalence, i.e. the level-1 source carries no item text at either level. A shell table carrying nothing but the instrument name would make this count as 'has item text' in the corpus figures while giving a reader no wording at all, which is the #1770 test failing (no row would carry the item's referent beyond what the item code and the table name already say). RETRY TEST: NO -- determinate. This is not an access failure; every source was retrieved successfully and the verdict is that the wording does not exist to be published. What would have to change: the RAVLT trial-by-trial examiner script as administered in Italian would have to be published somewhere authoritative AND a ruling that whole-task examiner instructions belong on a table whose items are trials and whose responses are error counts. Third-party Italian renderings of the Carlesimo et al. (1996) instructions circulate on lecture-notes sites, but the study never states which manual's script was read, and a level-4 reproduction of uncertain fidelity is not a literal transcript.
